prechecks_without_validator.refuses_with: Can only assert expertise backed by your own WorldlineTrace.
prechecks_without_validator.verdict: courtesy, deliberately — already decided in the source
prechecks_without_validator.reading: NOT A GAP, and it was never an open question: the twelve lines above this check say so explicitly ("A COURTESY, NOT AN ENFORCED RULE, and deliberately so"), name the reason, and state the condition for revisiting. What it builds is an ordinary Claim, so validate_claim governs it and has no notion of traces; a client bypassing the extern can cite anybody's. That is tolerable because an expertise assertion carries NO STANDING — a self-asserted, critiquable Claim in a non-authoritative index. SPEC §5.21. THE REVISIT TRIGGER IS WRITTEN INTO THE COMMENT: any future mechanism that gives these claims weight has to add the validation first.

prechecks_without_validator.verdict: no twin is POSSIBLE, and the condition is the wrong boundary
prechecks_without_validator.reading: A TWIN CANNOT EXIST HERE AT ANY protocol_version. The field lives in SealedPrediction, this zome's only private entry, and the integrity zome already says at the arm where the rule would go that "a private entry's content is not available here" — hdi delivers None for the body. So no peer ever sees the prediction at commit time. The content IS public at reveal, so the rule could in principle live in validate_revelation instead — and should not, for two measured reasons. (1) "Not empty" is a proxy for "not vacuous" and the proxy does not hold: `prediction: "."` is accepted, revealed, and lands in get_foresight_record's `revealed` list indistinguishably from a real kept commitment. A rule would refuse the one input nobody would ever use. (2) NOTHING COUNTS revealed commitments — no `.revealed.length` anywhere in the UI, the SDK or the MCP server; every surface renders the prediction's own text, and the foresight tab says in its intro that there is no score on the page. The inflation a vacuous reveal would cause has no consumer. Leave as a courtesy; spend no bump.

prechecks_without_validator.refuses_with: salt must not be empty; without it a guessable prediction is recoverable from its hash
prechecks_without_validator.verdict: no twin is possible, and the check's own purpose is not a rule
prechecks_without_validator.reading: Same impossibility as the prediction check — private entry, content is None in validation. But this one fails at its OWN STATED PURPOSE in a way worth recording, because it is the item-14 shape again. The message says the salt exists so "a guessable prediction is [not] recoverable from its hash", and `salt: "."` is accepted: a one-character salt is as brute-forcible as none, so the check does not achieve what it claims even in the coordinator. THE ACHIEVABLE VERSION IS AN ENTROPY REQUIREMENT, AND NO VALIDATION RULE CAN CHECK ONE — entropy is a property of the process that generated a string, not of the string, so a validator cannot tell a well-chosen salt from a badly chosen one by inspection. Like reveal_deadline needing a clock hdi does not have, this is a goal that is not expressible as a deterministic rule over the data. And the exposure is the COMMITTER'S OWN: a weak salt makes their own commitment recoverable and misleads nobody else. Leave as a courtesy; spend no bump.
